prompt.context: Our client, Shermer Pharma, is a venture-backed start-up pharmaceutical company. Over the past 15 years, Shermer has been developing a molecule that has been approved by the FDA to cure Alzheimer's with 90% efficacy. Shermer has no existing Sales or Marketing organization — the company has purely been a research firm to this point. The product is a pill that cures Alzheimer's, an illness that currently has no treatment that cures or stops the progress of the disease. Alzheimer's is a degenerative, terminal disease that causes senility and dementia. The client sells to Neurologists and Psychiatrists (not directly to consumers). Shermer will be the only firm with a cure for the next 5 years due to barriers to competition.
prompt.question: Shermer Pharma needs your help answering two questions: (1) How should we sell our product? (2) Is our product going to be profitable?

clarifying_info.q: How large is the Alzheimer's market?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 30 million people suffer worldwide. For the U.S. market you may size it yourself, but the actual U.S. patient population is 5 million.

clarifying_info.q: Does Shermer have any existing sales or marketing capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: No. Shermer has been purely a research firm. FDA approval has already been granted.

clarifying_info.q: Who are our target customers / who do we sell to?
clarifying_info.a: Sales would be focused on Neurologists and Psychiatrists — not directly to consumers.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors we need to worry about?
clarifying_info.a: We will not focus on competitive response; Shermer is the only firm with a cure and will be for the next 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the product?
clarifying_info.a: The annual gross margin per user is $1,000 (manufacturing and packaging costs are already included in this gross margin figure).
Total R&D costs are $1.5 billion, which must be fully recovered by Year 5 (straight-line amortization over 5 years, ignoring NPV).
G&A costs are $25 million per year.
We can ignore taxes for this analysis, though a strong candidate will ask about it.

exhibits.title: Sales Force Options
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of two sales channel options: Develop Own Sales Force vs. Contract Sales Force. Rows include: Percent of visit focused on our product, Fully loaded annual cost of 1 sales rep, Cost per sales call, Total calls required, Total Sales Reps needed, and Total Annual Selling Cost. Some cells are blank and must be calculated.

exhibits.title: Annual Net Income
exhibits.shows: A 5-year P&L table with rows for Projected Market Penetration, Total Users, Total Gross Margin, Amortized R&D Costs, Selling Costs, G&A Costs, and Net Income. Market penetration percentages are given for each year; all dollar figures are blank and must be calculated by the candidate.

framework: Go-to-Market / Sales Channel: How will Shermer build or acquire sales capability — own sales force, contract sales, or sell the company to a larger firm?
Market Sizing: How large is the addressable Alzheimer's patient population in the U.S.?
Revenue Model: What is the price per patient and how does market penetration ramp over time?
Cost Structure: What are R&D (amortized), selling, and G&A costs under each sales channel option?
Profitability: Can Shermer recover R&D costs and achieve positive net income by Year 5?
Risk & Qualitative Factors: Effectiveness of contract vs. own sales force; option to sell company; regulatory/competitive considerations

questions.prompt: Which sales channel option should Shermer choose, and why? Use Exhibit 1 to compare the financial cost of each option.
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify three options: (1) own sales force, (2) contract sales, (3) sell the company. For Exhibit 1 the candidate must calculate missing cells. Own sales force: cost per call = $200k / (100k calls/85 reps) = $170/call (alternatively: $200k fully loaded / ~1,176 calls per rep). Total annual selling cost = 85 reps x $200k = $17MM. Contract sales force: since only 50% of the visit is focused on the product, twice as many calls are needed — 200k calls total. Reps needed = 200k/100k x 85 = 170 reps equivalent. Total annual selling cost = 200k calls x $60/call = $12MM. Contract sales is $5MM cheaper per year. The qualitative caveat is that contract sales is typically less effective than an internal force (reps also sell competing products). Selling the company is a valid third option but no financial data is provided.

math.setup: Own Sales Force: 85 reps x $200k/rep. Contract: 100k calls (base) / 50% focus = 200k calls needed; 200k calls x $60/call.
math.answer: Contract sales force saves ~$5MM per year vs. own sales force; contract sales is the recommended channel on financial grounds.

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the U.S. Alzheimer's patient market (optional brain teaser before Exhibit 2).
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a top-down estimate: U.S. population ~330M, skewed older. Alzheimer's primarily affects people 65+. Roughly 15% of U.S. population is 65+ (~50M). Prevalence among 65+ is ~10%, yielding ~5M patients. The interviewer confirms the actual number is 5 million.

math.setup: U.S. population x share aged 65+ x Alzheimer's prevalence among 65+
math.answer: ~5 million U.S. Alzheimer's patients (confirmed by interviewer)

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, build the 5-year P&L for Shermer assuming contract sales. Is the product profitable? Does Shermer recover R&D costs by Year 5?
questions.guidance: Candidate must populate the blank Exhibit 2 table using: Total market = 5MM patients; gross margin = $1,000/patient; R&D = $1.5B amortized straight-line over 5 years = $300MM/year; selling cost = $12MM/year (contract); G&A = $25MM/year. Calculate each year's Total Users = 5MM x penetration %. Gross Margin = users x $1,000. Net Income = Gross Margin - $300MM R&D - $12MM selling - $25MM G&A.

math.setup: Total Users = 5,000,000 x market penetration. Total Gross Margin = Total Users x $1,000. Net Income = Gross Margin - $300MM (R&D amort) - $12MM (selling) - $25MM (G&A).
steps: Cumulative Net Income Y1-Y5: -$87MM+$163MM+$913MM+$1,663MM+$2,663MM = $5,315MM (well above $0 by Y5)
math.answer: Shermer is unprofitable in Year 1 (-$87MM) but achieves profitability from Year 2 onward and cumulatively recovers all R&D costs well before Year 5. The product is highly profitable.

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors or risks should Shermer consider as it moves forward with a contract sales launch?

categories.name: Sales Force Effectiveness
ideas: Contract sales reps also represent other products — divided attention may reduce effectiveness
An internal sales force may generate higher revenue but costs $5MM more annually
Building internal capability could be a longer-term strategic investment

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: At $1,000/year, the product may be underpriced for a life-saving cure to a currently incurable disease
Pricing power may allow significant upside; reimbursement dynamics with insurers/Medicare should be explored
Price sensitivity among patients, payers, and physicians should be assessed

categories.name: Market Access & Reimbursement
ideas: Medicare/Medicaid coverage decisions will drive volume significantly
Prior authorization requirements could slow patient uptake
Patient assistance programs for uninsured populations

categories.name: Competitive Risk
ideas: 5-year competitive window is finite; Shermer should maximize penetration before generics/biosimilars enter
Licensing or partnerships could accelerate market development

categories.name: Strategic Alternatives
ideas: Selling the company to a larger pharma firm with existing sales infrastructure may maximize value for shareholders
A partnership or co-promotion deal could provide capital and sales reach without full acquisition
Remaining independent preserves upside but requires building organizational capabilities from scratch

categories.name: Operational / Execution Risks
ideas: Manufacturing scale-up to serve millions of patients
Supply chain reliability for a life-saving drug

recommendation: Shermer Pharma should launch its Alzheimer's cure using a contract sales organization targeting Neurologists and Psychiatrists, as this channel costs $12MM per year versus $17MM for an internal sales force — saving $5MM annually while avoiding the need to build a sales organization from scratch.
The product will be profitable: Shermer reaches positive net income by Year 2 and cumulatively recovers the $1.5B R&D investment well before Year 5.

Selling the company to a larger pharmaceutical firm is also a strong option that should be presented to ownership — it would realize value immediately, leverage an acquirer's existing sales infrastructure, and eliminate execution risk.
risks: Contract sales reps have divided attention (50% focus on Shermer's product) which may reduce effectiveness and slow market penetration relative to projections
Year 1 net income is negative (-$87MM), requiring adequate cash reserves or continued venture backing
The 5-year competitive window is finite; failure to achieve penetration targets before competitors enter would materially reduce long-term value
Current pricing of ~$1,000/year may be leaving significant value on the table for a life-saving, first-in-class cure
next_steps: Negotiate a contract sales agreement and align on territory coverage, rep incentive structure, and performance metrics
Evaluate acquisition or partnership offers from major pharmaceutical companies to assess whether selling creates more value than independent launch
Conduct payer/reimbursement analysis to confirm Medicare and private insurer coverage and model realistic net pricing
Stress-test the financial model under lower penetration scenarios to ensure the company has sufficient runway through Year 1 losses
